column1: # Standing gate rules. Every step's rules file includes this one.
# Nothing here is about a particular Spark version. These are the rules that
# say the four instruments actually ran and that the tree they read is one a
# human would accept -- a tree that parses, a build that resolves, a job that
# started. A step-specific rule that came back PASS over a tree whose POM did
# not resolve would be measuring nothing, so these run first and their failure
# is meant to be read as "the reading is void", not "the candidate is wrong".
# The last two implement rule 11's "count suppressions as findings". The
# baseline carries exactly ten @SuppressWarnings, six `resource` and four
# `rawtypes` (NOTES 4.8.1); none of them silences a deprecation. An agent that
# answers a deprecation warning with an annotation instead of a call change has
# not migrated anything, and the budget catches the general case of the same
# move under any other warning name.
# `probe-ran` keys on app.id and not on spark.version because spark.version is
# read off the session and 62 of this codebase's 78 mains never make one
# (NOTES 4.8.7). app.id is emitted from the application-start callback whatever
# the job is, so the rule says "a job ran and the listener was on it" and
# nothing more -- which is all a standing rule can honestly say here.
# `probe-submit-ok` is the rest of that sentence, and it is here because a run
# went green without it. A job that builds a session and then dies on its first
# read still emits app.id: the first real step-1 verifier run had submit.rc 1,
# zero Spark jobs started, and a `probe-ran` that passed. app.id says a session
# existed; submit.rc says the job the probe was pointed at finished. A gate that
# reads the first as the second is reporting facts gathered from a process that
# crashed, which is the definition of a void reading.
# id
ast-parses
column5: the source tree does not parse, or the scanner that reads it did not run; either way every ast rule below is void

column1: pom-resolves
column5: Maven could not produce an effective POM or a dependency list

column1: classes-readable
column5: a class file under target/ could not be read

column1: probe-clean
column5: the in-job probe reported an error instead of a reading

column1: ast-nonempty
column5: fewer than 200 source files were scanned; the scan did not see the tree

column1: classes-nonempty

column1: probe-ran
column5: the job never started, or the probe was not attached to it

column1: probe-submit-ok
column5: the probe's job did not exit 0; every fact beside this one came from a job that failed

column1: no-deprecation-suppression
column5: a deprecation warning was silenced with an annotation rather than answered

column1: suppression-budget
column5: more @SuppressWarnings than the ten the baseline carries
